argument:
Ran the pair and my coverage against the thesis. Three problems, one concession.

1) The ratio itself carries no edge. Verified via pair-ratio: EWC/ACWI 0.3797, 62.3rd percentile — but z-score is only +0.33. That is a mid-range reading, not a mispricing. The percentile framing ('room to the 0.3993 high') describes a range, not a signal. Meanwhile EWC has already outperformed ACWI by ~7pts over 1Y (+32.4% vs +25.3%) and +2.9pts over 1M (+5.7% vs +2.8%, returns verified) — i.e., a meaningful chunk of the crude spike (+8.5% 1m) is already in the ratio. This is a momentum entry at mid-range on a headline-driven commodity premium, not variant perception at a dislocation.

2) The 'uncrowded alternative to IWD/IWF' claim measures crowding on the wrong instrument. Short ACWI is ~65% short the US, and the US weight is dominated by the mega-cap growth/ad complex — the same growth-short factor that sits at the 94th percentile in IWD/IWF. My coverage confirms the factor is already working: XLC +0.7% 1M, -5.0% 3M; META -12.5% 3M. EWC/ACWI being at its own 62nd percentile doesn't make the exposure uncrowded — the return driver is the same trade, entered through a correlated wrapper. If value/growth mean-reverts off the 94th percentile on a ceasefire or soft CPI, this pair bleeds through the identical channel.

3) The CAD-hike leg is internally contradictory on EWC's construction. Financials are the index's largest sector (~33%, RY/TD/BNS heavy); energy is only ~17-18%. A hawkish BoC — the base case's policy confirmation — directly pressures the banks through the mortgage-renewal wall the proposal itself flags. The thesis needs the BoC hawkish enough to carry CAD but not hawkish enough to crack housing; that is a narrow corridor to rest a 55% base case on.

Concession: if the regime call is right (inflation scare, two-sided hike risk), the short ACWI leg is well-chosen — ad budgets are the first line item cut in a stagflation scare, and the ad-platform complex is already de-rating (numbers above). The hedge genuinely expresses the regime.

Net: the macro regime read may be sound, but the instrument selection argument — the core of the pitch — is weak. You're buying a mid-range ratio after a year of outperformance, on a single-commodity flip condition (Brent <$72), with a -2.7% stop that a Sunday-night ceasefire gap in Brent will not honor. Conviction 6 is fair-to-generous; I'd score it 5 until the ratio offers an actual dislocation entry or the thesis survives a crude pullback to $75 intact.
